name: LCC International University
summary: Klaipeda university where all courses are taught in English: seven BA majors and students from 50+ countries.

ib.text: Completing the IB or European Baccalaureate replaces the English test. Admission scores your last three school years (40%), English (30%) and an interview (30%). No subject requirements.

lastYear.text: early 15 Feb; EU and visa-free 15 July

programmes.name: International Business Administration
programmes.about: Business degree focused on European and global economies: management, marketing and accounting, with supervised work experience in real business settings.
programmes.overview: The four years move from critical thinking and business fundamentals through management functions, accounting, marketing and information systems to business research, organisational behaviour and electives in economics, marketing or leadership. Core courses include micro- and macroeconomics, financial and management accounting, statistics, business finance and entrepreneurship, with a focus on the European and global economy and Eastern Europe in particular. A supervised business practicum in year four and a thesis defended in public finish the degree. Graduates move into management, finance, marketing, human resources or their own enterprise, or on to graduate study.
programmes.selectionNote: Score is your last three school years 40%, an English test 30% and an interview 30%; an IB Diploma replaces the English test. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.

programmes.name: Global Business and Communication
programmes.about: Business management blended with communication: influencing consumers, growing brands and communicating across cultures.
programmes.overview: Business management courses (financial accounting, marketing, business finance, economics) sit beside liberal arts courses in arts, history, natural sciences and ethics, and communication electives such as media literacy, public relations, web and graphic design, social media management, brand management and marketing communication. Classes are small, with about sixteen students per teacher, and the emphasis is on practical experience. The degree blends creativity with business management for careers in marketing, social media and digital marketing, product and brand management and public relations.
programmes.selectionNote: Score is your last three school years 40%, an English test 30% and an interview 30%; an IB Diploma replaces the English test. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.

programmes.name: Contemporary Communication
programmes.about: Public relations, advertising, social media, media production and business communication, with video production and persuasion skills from year one.
programmes.overview: The curriculum spans communication and media fundamentals, interpersonal communication, video production, media theory, public relations, media writing, web design, rhetorical analysis, persuasion and propaganda, cultural communication and conflict resolution, with leadership and ethics throughout. You make video productions, complete an internship in year four with a local or international business, and carry out a capstone project on a communication theme of your choice. Classes are small. Graduates work in public relations, advertising, social media, government and business communication, media production and NGOs, or continue to graduate study in communication.
programmes.selectionNote: Score is your last three school years 40%, an English test 30% and an interview 30%; an IB Diploma replaces the English test. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.

programmes.name: English Language and Literature
programmes.about: Language study (phonetics, syntax, psycholinguistics), literature, translation and interpretation, research methods and a practicum in translation, literacy or teaching.
programmes.overview: Core courses cover written composition, literature, linguistics, TESOL methods, translation and interpretation, expository writing, language research methods and ethics, set within a liberal arts frame that includes world civilizations. Workshops and writing assignments are complemented by practicum courses such as teaching in summer camps or schools, editorial work or submitting literary work for publication. In year four you write a thesis with a faculty mentor and defend it in public. Tracks lean toward English teaching, translation and literary studies, and graduates work in teaching, translation, marketing and administration or continue to graduate study.
programmes.selectionNote: Score is your last three school years 40%, an English test 30% and an interview 30%; an IB Diploma replaces the English test. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.

programmes.name: International Relations and Development
programmes.about: International relations for careers in government or development NGOs: political theory, development cooperation, conflict resolution and research methods.
programmes.overview: You study political science, international relations, development theory, economics and research methodology, together with political philosophy, conflict studies, negotiation, project management and intercultural communication. Research is built in from the start: a research proposal in year one, primary data collection in years three and four, and an independent thesis project at the end. Two supervised practicum courses place you in real-world work settings. Classes are small. Graduates work in diplomatic missions, public institutions, NGOs, development cooperation, human rights organisations and research institutes, or continue to graduate study.
programmes.selectionNote: Score is your last three school years 40%, an English test 30% and an interview 30%; an IB Diploma replaces the English test. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.

programmes.name: Psychology
programmes.about: Psychology for human-service and health careers or further clinical and research study, ending in an original research thesis defended in public.
programmes.overview: The four years run from introduction to psychology, human development and interpersonal communication, through social and biological psychology, research methods and statistics, health psychology, cognition and introduction to clinical psychology, to abnormal psychology, counselling, neuropsychology, psychological assessment, then educational and organisational psychology. Practicum I in year two and a supervised Practicum II in an approved agency in year four give field experience, and an individual research thesis closes the degree. Graduates go into graduate study in clinical, counselling, educational or organisational psychology and neuropsychology, or work in social services, human resources and education.
programmes.selectionNote: Score is your last three school years 40%, an English test 30% and an interview 30%; an IB Diploma replaces the English test. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.

programmes.name: Evangelical Theology
programmes.about: Biblical studies, theology and philosophy with Christian life and ministry courses, for church leadership and careers in education and business.
programmes.overview: The programme centres on biblical literature (Old and New Testament, the Pentateuch, the Synoptic Gospels), Christian theology, the history of Christianity, apologetics and worldview, with philosophy, ethics, missiology, peacemaking and justice. First-year seminars are interactive and group-based, two Christian ministry practicum courses come with instructor guidance, and year four includes research methods and a supervised thesis defended in public. Classes are small. Graduates are prepared for theological graduate study, ministry in churches and service organisations, teaching, or professional careers that draw on a liberal arts education.
programmes.selectionNote: Score is your last three school years 40%, an English test 30% and an interview 30%; an IB Diploma replaces the English test. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.

notes: Tuition is €4,290 a year for every student, EU or not; EU citizens can also claim the Lithuanian government study stipend and loans, and about half of students get financial aid.
Applying early helps: early deadlines come in February, and LCC gives conditional acceptance from December on English and interview results before exams are finished.
Every major is also offered with a January start; the catalogue lists seven majors while the website describes the business major as Global Business and Communication.
